title: 1  dmr_rasher_steneck
section: 2.4 How Does the Data Fit Into the Long-Term Trend Analysis?
text:
2.4 How Does the Data Fit Into the Long-Term Trend Analysis?
We fit two models. One where the slope varies by ecoregion (note: the GOSL and Newfoundland are collapsed) and one where the slope does not vary by ecoregion. Based on the modeled results, here is the smoothed fits to your data. Note - the model with a common slope appears to best predict (best fit in terms of prediction and p-value for slope*ecoregion is not distinguishable from 0).
Note - the study (black) line might not line up in the middle or on trajectories, as it is shrunken in towards the grand mean for the ecoregion.

2.4.1 3.1 Slope Varying by Ecoregion Model


Show the code
mod_ecoregion <- readRDS(here::here("models/mod_ecoregion.rds"))


# for plotting to do the back transform
exp_trans <- function(dat){

  dat |>
    mutate(
      Predicted = exp(Predicted)-0.01,
           CI_low = exp(CI_low)-0.01,
           CI_high = exp(CI_high)-0.01,
           CI_high = ifelse(CI_high>1.1, 1.1, CI_high)
    )|>
               mutate(trajectory = 
                        gsub(study[1], "", trajectory))

}


re_ecoregion <- ranef(mod_ecoregion)$cond$study |>
  as_tibble(rownames = "study")  |> 
  filter(study == params$dataset_name) |> 
  pull(`(Intercept)`)


dat_fixed_ecoregion <- estimate_relation(mod_ecoregion,
                               include_random = FALSE,
                  length = 200,
                  data = kelptime_study) |>
  mutate(Predicted = Predicted + re_ecoregion,
         CI_high = CI_high + re_ecoregion,
         CI_low = CI_low + re_ecoregion) |>
  exp_trans()

dat_traj_ecoregion <- estimate_relation(mod_ecoregion,
                              include_random = TRUE,
                  length = 200,
                  data = kelptime_study) |>
    exp_trans()


ggplot(dat_traj_ecoregion, aes(x = year)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Predicted,
                color = trajectory), alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_point(aes(y = focal_std_by_ecoregion,
                 group = trajectory,
                 color = trajectory), alpha = 0.5,
             data = kelptime_study |>
               mutate(trajectory = 
                        gsub(study[1], "", trajectory))) +
  geom_line(data = dat_fixed_ecoregion,
            aes(y = Predicted), color = "black") +
  geom_ribbon(data = dat_fixed_ecoregion,
            aes(y = Predicted,
                ymin = CI_low,
                ymax = CI_high), color = NA,
            alpha = 0.4) +
  labs(x = "", y = "Standardized Kelp",
      color = "site") +
  guides(color = "none")











2.4.2 3.2 Common Slope Model


Show the code
mod_common_slope <- readRDS(here::here("models/mod_common_slope.rds"))

re <- ranef(mod_common_slope)$cond$study |>
  as_tibble(rownames = "study")  |> 
  filter(study == params$dataset_name) |> 
  pull(`(Intercept)`)


dat_fixed <- estimate_relation(mod_common_slope,
                               include_random = FALSE,
                  length = 200,
                  data = kelptime_study) |>
  mutate(Predicted = Predicted + re,
         CI_high = CI_high + re_ecoregion,
         CI_low = CI_low + re_ecoregion) |>
  exp_trans()

dat_traj <- estimate_relation(mod_common_slope,
                              include_random = TRUE,
                  length = 200,
                  data = kelptime_study) |>
    exp_trans()

ggplot(dat_traj, aes(x = year)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Predicted,
                color = trajectory), alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_point(aes(y = focal_std_by_ecoregion,
                 group = trajectory,
                 color = trajectory), alpha = 0.5,
             data = kelptime_study |>
               mutate(trajectory = 
                        gsub(study[1], "", trajectory))) +
  geom_line(data = dat_fixed,
            aes(y = Predicted), color = "black") +
  geom_ribbon(data = dat_fixed,
            aes(y = Predicted,
                ymin = CI_low,
                ymax = CI_high), color = NA,
            alpha = 0.4) +
  labs(x = "", y = "Standardized Kelp",
      color = "site") +
  guides(color = "none")

section: 2.5 How Does the Data Fit Into the Spatially Varying Trend Analysis?
text:
2.5 How Does the Data Fit Into the Spatially Varying Trend Analysis?
First, let’s look at the map showing slopes for each site.


Show the code
fitted_spatial_predictions <- readRDS(here::here("data/model_derived_data/fitted_spatial_model_sf.rds")) |>
  filter(study == params$dataset_name)

slopes_spatial_fits <- 
  fitted_spatial_predictions |>
  group_by(trajectory) |>
  slice(1L) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(trajectory, latitude, eco_collapsed, combined_slope_median:combined_slope_upr) |>
  arrange(combined_slope_mean) |>
  mutate(samp = 1:n()) |>
  st_transform(4326) |>
  mutate(text = glue("slope = {round(combined_slope_mean,4)}"))




Show the code
domain <- c(-1*max(abs(slopes_spatial_fits$combined_slope_mean)),
               max(abs(slopes_spatial_fits$combined_slope_mean)))

spatial_slope_pal <- 
  colorNumeric(
    colorspace::divergingx_hcl(7,
                               palette = "RdYlBu"),
    domain = domain)

leaflet() |>
  addTiles() |>
  addCircleMarkers(data = slopes_spatial_fits,
             fillColor = ~spatial_slope_pal(combined_slope_mean),
             fillOpacity = 0.8,
             popup = ~text,
             stroke = 0) |>
   addLegend(pal =spatial_slope_pal,
             values = seq(domain[1], domain[2], length.out = 7) )






Next, let’s see how that actually plays out on a scatter plot with individual fit lines overlain. Note, colors go from south to north.


Show the code
ggplot(fitted_spatial_predictions,
         aes(x = year,
             y = exp(est)-0.01,
             color = latitude,
             group = trajectory,
         )) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1.1, alpha = 0.9) +
    labs(y = "Standardized Kelp Abundance", x = "",
         color = "Latitude") +
    theme_bw(base_size = 14)+
    scale_colour_distiller(palette = "RdBu", direction = 1) +
    geom_point(aes(y = yi), alpha = 0.4) +
    facet_wrap(vars(eco_collapsed))









The above shows the results directly from the fit model for the individual data sets. These model, however, has a random effect for each site. Let’s instead show a map of the region with the general trends from the region from the model fit.
Note - circle markers with an outline around them are estimates from the model for observed sites. Other points are from a grid around the region and represent model estimates for those sites.


Show the code
spatial_predictions <- readRDS(here::here("data/model_derived_data/prediction_spatial_model_sf.rds")) 

# crop to extent of dataset
spatial_predictions <- spatial_predictions |> 
  st_crop(st_bbox(fitted_spatial_predictions) |>st_as_sfc() |> st_buffer(1e1))


Warning: attribute variables are assumed to be spatially constant throughout
all geometries


Show the code
slopes_spatial_predictions <- 
  spatial_predictions |>
  group_by(X, Y) |>
  slice(1L) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(X, Y, combined_slope_median:combined_slope_upr) |>
  arrange(combined_slope_mean) |>
  mutate(samp = 1:n()) |>
  st_transform(4326) |>
  mutate(text = glue("slope = {round(combined_slope_mean,4)}"))




Show the code
domain <- c(-1*max(abs(slopes_spatial_predictions$combined_slope_mean)),
               max(abs(slopes_spatial_predictions$combined_slope_mean)))

spatial_slope_pal <- 
  colorNumeric(
    colorspace::divergingx_hcl(7,
                               palette = "RdYlBu"),
    domain = domain)

leaflet() |>
  addTiles() |>
  addCircleMarkers(data = slopes_spatial_predictions,
             fillColor = ~spatial_slope_pal(combined_slope_mean),
             fillOpacity = 0.8,
             popup = ~text,
             stroke = 0) |>
    addCircleMarkers(data = slopes_spatial_fits,
             fillColor = ~spatial_slope_pal(combined_slope_mean),
             fillOpacity = 0.8,
             popup = ~text,
             stroke = 1) |>
   addLegend(pal =spatial_slope_pal,
             values = seq(domain[1], domain[2], length.out = 7) )






Last, let’s show the data set, but the curves show the regional fits - again, colors go south to north.


Show the code
spatial_curves <- readRDS(here::here("data/model_derived_data/prediction_spatial_model_curves.rds")) |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("X", "Y"), 
           crs = st_crs(spatial_predictions),
           remove = FALSE)|> 
  # crop to the dataset
  st_crop(st_bbox(fitted_spatial_predictions) |>st_as_sfc() |> st_buffer(1e1)) |>
  st_transform(4326) %>%
    mutate(lon = sf::st_coordinates(.)[,1],
                lat = sf::st_coordinates(.)[,2]) |>
  # Trim to the time of the data set
  filter(year >= min(study_data$Sample.Year)) |>
  filter(year <= max(study_data$Sample.Year))


Warning: attribute variables are assumed to be spatially constant throughout
all geometries


Show the code
ggplot(fitted_spatial_predictions,
       aes(x = year, color = latitude,
                    y = yi)) +
  geom_point( alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_line(data = spatial_curves,
            aes(y = est, 
                color = lat,
                group = Y))  +
  scale_color_viridis_c() +
  labs(y="", x = "Standardized Kelp Abundance", 
       color = "Latitude")

title: 2  Godbout_StLawrence
section: 3.4 How Does the Data Fit Into the Long-Term Trend Analysis?
text:
3.4 How Does the Data Fit Into the Long-Term Trend Analysis?
We fit two models. One where the slope varies by ecoregion (note: the GOSL and Newfoundland are collapsed) and one where the slope does not vary by ecoregion. Based on the modeled results, here is the smoothed fits to your data. Note - the model with a common slope appears to best predict (best fit in terms of prediction and p-value for slope*ecoregion is not distinguishable from 0).
Note - the study (black) line might not line up in the middle or on trajectories, as it is shrunken in towards the grand mean for the ecoregion.

3.4.1 3.1 Slope Varying by Ecoregion Model


Show the code
mod_ecoregion <- readRDS(here::here("models/mod_ecoregion.rds"))


# for plotting to do the back transform
exp_trans <- function(dat){

  dat |>
    mutate(
      Predicted = exp(Predicted)-0.01,
           CI_low = exp(CI_low)-0.01,
           CI_high = exp(CI_high)-0.01,
           CI_high = ifelse(CI_high>1.1, 1.1, CI_high)
    )|>
               mutate(trajectory = 
                        gsub(study[1], "", trajectory))

}


re_ecoregion <- ranef(mod_ecoregion)$cond$study |>
  as_tibble(rownames = "study")  |> 
  filter(study == params$dataset_name) |> 
  pull(`(Intercept)`)


dat_fixed_ecoregion <- estimate_relation(mod_ecoregion,
                               include_random = FALSE,
                  length = 200,
                  data = kelptime_study) |>
  mutate(Predicted = Predicted + re_ecoregion,
         CI_high = CI_high + re_ecoregion,
         CI_low = CI_low + re_ecoregion) |>
  exp_trans()

dat_traj_ecoregion <- estimate_relation(mod_ecoregion,
                              include_random = TRUE,
                  length = 200,
                  data = kelptime_study) |>
    exp_trans()


ggplot(dat_traj_ecoregion, aes(x = year)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Predicted,
                color = trajectory), alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_point(aes(y = focal_std_by_ecoregion,
                 group = trajectory,
                 color = trajectory), alpha = 0.5,
             data = kelptime_study |>
               mutate(trajectory = 
                        gsub(study[1], "", trajectory))) +
  geom_line(data = dat_fixed_ecoregion,
            aes(y = Predicted), color = "black") +
  geom_ribbon(data = dat_fixed_ecoregion,
            aes(y = Predicted,
                ymin = CI_low,
                ymax = CI_high), color = NA,
            alpha = 0.4) +
  labs(x = "", y = "Standardized Kelp",
      color = "site") +
  guides(color = "none")











3.4.2 3.2 Common Slope Model


Show the code
mod_common_slope <- readRDS(here::here("models/mod_common_slope.rds"))

re <- ranef(mod_common_slope)$cond$study |>
  as_tibble(rownames = "study")  |> 
  filter(study == params$dataset_name) |> 
  pull(`(Intercept)`)


dat_fixed <- estimate_relation(mod_common_slope,
                               include_random = FALSE,
                  length = 200,
                  data = kelptime_study) |>
  mutate(Predicted = Predicted + re,
         CI_high = CI_high + re_ecoregion,
         CI_low = CI_low + re_ecoregion) |>
  exp_trans()

dat_traj <- estimate_relation(mod_common_slope,
                              include_random = TRUE,
                  length = 200,
                  data = kelptime_study) |>
    exp_trans()

ggplot(dat_traj, aes(x = year)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Predicted,
                color = trajectory), alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_point(aes(y = focal_std_by_ecoregion,
                 group = trajectory,
                 color = trajectory), alpha = 0.5,
             data = kelptime_study |>
               mutate(trajectory = 
                        gsub(study[1], "", trajectory))) +
  geom_line(data = dat_fixed,
            aes(y = Predicted), color = "black") +
  geom_ribbon(data = dat_fixed,
            aes(y = Predicted,
                ymin = CI_low,
                ymax = CI_high), color = NA,
            alpha = 0.4) +
  labs(x = "", y = "Standardized Kelp",
      color = "site") +
  guides(color = "none")

section: 3.5 How Does the Data Fit Into the Spatially Varying Trend Analysis?
text:
3.5 How Does the Data Fit Into the Spatially Varying Trend Analysis?
First, let’s look at the map showing slopes for each site.


Show the code
fitted_spatial_predictions <- readRDS(here::here("data/model_derived_data/fitted_spatial_model_sf.rds")) |>
  filter(study == params$dataset_name)

slopes_spatial_fits <- 
  fitted_spatial_predictions |>
  group_by(trajectory) |>
  slice(1L) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(trajectory, latitude, eco_collapsed, combined_slope_median:combined_slope_upr) |>
  arrange(combined_slope_mean) |>
  mutate(samp = 1:n()) |>
  st_transform(4326) |>
  mutate(text = glue("slope = {round(combined_slope_mean,4)}"))




Show the code
domain <- c(-1*max(abs(slopes_spatial_fits$combined_slope_mean)),
               max(abs(slopes_spatial_fits$combined_slope_mean)))

spatial_slope_pal <- 
  colorNumeric(
    colorspace::divergingx_hcl(7,
                               palette = "RdYlBu"),
    domain = domain)

leaflet() |>
  addTiles() |>
  addCircleMarkers(data = slopes_spatial_fits,
             fillColor = ~spatial_slope_pal(combined_slope_mean),
             fillOpacity = 0.8,
             popup = ~text,
             stroke = 0) |>
   addLegend(pal =spatial_slope_pal,
             values = seq(domain[1], domain[2], length.out = 7) )






Next, let’s see how that actually plays out on a scatter plot with individual fit lines overlain. Note, colors go from south to north.


Show the code
ggplot(fitted_spatial_predictions,
         aes(x = year,
             y = exp(est)-0.01,
             color = latitude,
             group = trajectory,
         )) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1.1, alpha = 0.9) +
    labs(y = "Standardized Kelp Abundance", x = "",
         color = "Latitude") +
    theme_bw(base_size = 14)+
    scale_colour_distiller(palette = "RdBu", direction = 1) +
    geom_point(aes(y = yi), alpha = 0.4) +
    facet_wrap(vars(eco_collapsed))









The above shows the results directly from the fit model for the individual data sets. These model, however, has a random effect for each site. Let’s instead show a map of the region with the general trends from the region from the model fit.
Note - circle markers with an outline around them are estimates from the model for observed sites. Other points are from a grid around the region and represent model estimates for those sites.


Show the code
spatial_predictions <- readRDS(here::here("data/model_derived_data/prediction_spatial_model_sf.rds")) 

# crop to extent of dataset
spatial_predictions <- spatial_predictions |> 
  st_crop(st_bbox(fitted_spatial_predictions) |>st_as_sfc() |> st_buffer(1e1))


Warning: attribute variables are assumed to be spatially constant throughout
all geometries


Show the code
slopes_spatial_predictions <- 
  spatial_predictions |>
  group_by(X, Y) |>
  slice(1L) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(X, Y, combined_slope_median:combined_slope_upr) |>
  arrange(combined_slope_mean) |>
  mutate(samp = 1:n()) |>
  st_transform(4326) |>
  mutate(text = glue("slope = {round(combined_slope_mean,4)}"))




Show the code
domain <- c(-1*max(abs(slopes_spatial_predictions$combined_slope_mean)),
               max(abs(slopes_spatial_predictions$combined_slope_mean)))

spatial_slope_pal <- 
  colorNumeric(
    colorspace::divergingx_hcl(7,
                               palette = "RdYlBu"),
    domain = domain)

leaflet() |>
  addTiles() |>
  addCircleMarkers(data = slopes_spatial_predictions,
             fillColor = ~spatial_slope_pal(combined_slope_mean),
             fillOpacity = 0.8,
             popup = ~text,
             stroke = 0) |>
    addCircleMarkers(data = slopes_spatial_fits,
             fillColor = ~spatial_slope_pal(combined_slope_mean),
             fillOpacity = 0.8,
             popup = ~text,
             stroke = 1) |>
   addLegend(pal =spatial_slope_pal,
             values = seq(domain[1], domain[2], length.out = 7) )






Last, let’s show the data set, but the curves show the regional fits - again, colors go south to north.


Show the code
spatial_curves <- readRDS(here::here("data/model_derived_data/prediction_spatial_model_curves.rds")) |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("X", "Y"), 
           crs = st_crs(spatial_predictions),
           remove = FALSE)|> 
  # crop to the dataset
  st_crop(st_bbox(fitted_spatial_predictions) |>st_as_sfc() |> st_buffer(1e1)) |>
  st_transform(4326) %>%
    mutate(lon = sf::st_coordinates(.)[,1],
                lat = sf::st_coordinates(.)[,2]) |>
  # Trim to the time of the data set
  filter(year >= min(study_data$Sample.Year)) |>
  filter(year <= max(study_data$Sample.Year))


Warning: attribute variables are assumed to be spatially constant throughout
all geometries


Show the code
ggplot(fitted_spatial_predictions,
       aes(x = year, color = latitude,
                    y = yi)) +
  geom_point( alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_line(data = spatial_curves,
            aes(y = est, 
                color = lat,
                group = Y))  +
  scale_color_viridis_c() +
  labs(y="", x = "Standardized Kelp Abundance", 
       color = "Latitude")

section: 4.4 How Does the Data Fit Into the Long-Term Trend Analysis?
text:
4.4 How Does the Data Fit Into the Long-Term Trend Analysis?
We fit two models. One where the slope varies by ecoregion (note: the GOSL and Newfoundland are collapsed) and one where the slope does not vary by ecoregion. Based on the modeled results, here is the smoothed fits to your data. Note - the model with a common slope appears to best predict (best fit in terms of prediction and p-value for slope*ecoregion is not distinguishable from 0).
Note - the study (black) line might not line up in the middle or on trajectories, as it is shrunken in towards the grand mean for the ecoregion.

4.4.1 3.1 Slope Varying by Ecoregion Model


Show the code
mod_ecoregion <- readRDS(here::here("models/mod_ecoregion.rds"))


# for plotting to do the back transform
exp_trans <- function(dat){

  dat |>
    mutate(
      Predicted = exp(Predicted)-0.01,
           CI_low = exp(CI_low)-0.01,
           CI_high = exp(CI_high)-0.01,
           CI_high = ifelse(CI_high>1.1, 1.1, CI_high)
    )|>
               mutate(trajectory = 
                        gsub(study[1], "", trajectory))

}


re_ecoregion <- ranef(mod_ecoregion)$cond$study |>
  as_tibble(rownames = "study")  |> 
  filter(study == params$dataset_name) |> 
  pull(`(Intercept)`)


dat_fixed_ecoregion <- estimate_relation(mod_ecoregion,
                               include_random = FALSE,
                  length = 200,
                  data = kelptime_study) |>
  mutate(Predicted = Predicted + re_ecoregion,
         CI_high = CI_high + re_ecoregion,
         CI_low = CI_low + re_ecoregion) |>
  exp_trans()

dat_traj_ecoregion <- estimate_relation(mod_ecoregion,
                              include_random = TRUE,
                  length = 200,
                  data = kelptime_study) |>
    exp_trans()


ggplot(dat_traj_ecoregion, aes(x = year)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Predicted,
                color = trajectory), alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_point(aes(y = focal_std_by_ecoregion,
                 group = trajectory,
                 color = trajectory), alpha = 0.5,
             data = kelptime_study |>
               mutate(trajectory = 
                        gsub(study[1], "", trajectory))) +
  geom_line(data = dat_fixed_ecoregion,
            aes(y = Predicted), color = "black") +
  geom_ribbon(data = dat_fixed_ecoregion,
            aes(y = Predicted,
                ymin = CI_low,
                ymax = CI_high), color = NA,
            alpha = 0.4) +
  labs(x = "", y = "Standardized Kelp",
      color = "site") +
  guides(color = "none")











4.4.2 3.2 Common Slope Model


Show the code
mod_common_slope <- readRDS(here::here("models/mod_common_slope.rds"))

re <- ranef(mod_common_slope)$cond$study |>
  as_tibble(rownames = "study")  |> 
  filter(study == params$dataset_name) |> 
  pull(`(Intercept)`)


dat_fixed <- estimate_relation(mod_common_slope,
                               include_random = FALSE,
                  length = 200,
                  data = kelptime_study) |>
  mutate(Predicted = Predicted + re,
         CI_high = CI_high + re_ecoregion,
         CI_low = CI_low + re_ecoregion) |>
  exp_trans()

dat_traj <- estimate_relation(mod_common_slope,
                              include_random = TRUE,
                  length = 200,
                  data = kelptime_study) |>
    exp_trans()

ggplot(dat_traj, aes(x = year)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Predicted,
                color = trajectory), alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_point(aes(y = focal_std_by_ecoregion,
                 group = trajectory,
                 color = trajectory), alpha = 0.5,
             data = kelptime_study |>
               mutate(trajectory = 
                        gsub(study[1], "", trajectory))) +
  geom_line(data = dat_fixed,
            aes(y = Predicted), color = "black") +
  geom_ribbon(data = dat_fixed,
            aes(y = Predicted,
                ymin = CI_low,
                ymax = CI_high), color = NA,
            alpha = 0.4) +
  labs(x = "", y = "Standardized Kelp",
      color = "site") +
  guides(color = "none")

title: 3  gulf_of_maine_ios_southwestern_gom
section: 4.5 How Does the Data Fit Into the Spatially Varying Trend Analysis?
text:
4.5 How Does the Data Fit Into the Spatially Varying Trend Analysis?
First, let’s look at the map showing slopes for each site.


Show the code
fitted_spatial_predictions <- readRDS(here::here("data/model_derived_data/fitted_spatial_model_sf.rds")) |>
  filter(study == params$dataset_name)

slopes_spatial_fits <- 
  fitted_spatial_predictions |>
  group_by(trajectory) |>
  slice(1L) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(trajectory, latitude, eco_collapsed, combined_slope_median:combined_slope_upr) |>
  arrange(combined_slope_mean) |>
  mutate(samp = 1:n()) |>
  st_transform(4326) |>
  mutate(text = glue("slope = {round(combined_slope_mean,4)}"))




Show the code
domain <- c(-1*max(abs(slopes_spatial_fits$combined_slope_mean)),
               max(abs(slopes_spatial_fits$combined_slope_mean)))

spatial_slope_pal <- 
  colorNumeric(
    colorspace::divergingx_hcl(7,
                               palette = "RdYlBu"),
    domain = domain)

leaflet() |>
  addTiles() |>
  addCircleMarkers(data = slopes_spatial_fits,
             fillColor = ~spatial_slope_pal(combined_slope_mean),
             fillOpacity = 0.8,
             popup = ~text,
             stroke = 0) |>
   addLegend(pal =spatial_slope_pal,
             values = seq(domain[1], domain[2], length.out = 7) )






Next, let’s see how that actually plays out on a scatter plot with individual fit lines overlain. Note, colors go from south to north.


Show the code
ggplot(fitted_spatial_predictions,
         aes(x = year,
             y = exp(est)-0.01,
             color = latitude,
             group = trajectory,
         )) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1.1, alpha = 0.9) +
    labs(y = "Standardized Kelp Abundance", x = "",
         color = "Latitude") +
    theme_bw(base_size = 14)+
    scale_colour_distiller(palette = "RdBu", direction = 1) +
    geom_point(aes(y = yi), alpha = 0.4) +
    facet_wrap(vars(eco_collapsed))









The above shows the results directly from the fit model for the individual data sets. These model, however, has a random effect for each site. Let’s instead show a map of the region with the general trends from the region from the model fit.
Note - circle markers with an outline around them are estimates from the model for observed sites. Other points are from a grid around the region and represent model estimates for those sites.


Show the code
spatial_predictions <- readRDS(here::here("data/model_derived_data/prediction_spatial_model_sf.rds")) 

# crop to extent of dataset
spatial_predictions <- spatial_predictions |> 
  st_crop(st_bbox(fitted_spatial_predictions) |>st_as_sfc() |> st_buffer(1e1))


Warning: attribute variables are assumed to be spatially constant throughout
all geometries


Show the code
slopes_spatial_predictions <- 
  spatial_predictions |>
  group_by(X, Y) |>
  slice(1L) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(X, Y, combined_slope_median:combined_slope_upr) |>
  arrange(combined_slope_mean) |>
  mutate(samp = 1:n()) |>
  st_transform(4326) |>
  mutate(text = glue("slope = {round(combined_slope_mean,4)}"))




Show the code
domain <- c(-1*max(abs(slopes_spatial_predictions$combined_slope_mean)),
               max(abs(slopes_spatial_predictions$combined_slope_mean)))

spatial_slope_pal <- 
  colorNumeric(
    colorspace::divergingx_hcl(7,
                               palette = "RdYlBu"),
    domain = domain)

leaflet() |>
  addTiles() |>
  addCircleMarkers(data = slopes_spatial_predictions,
             fillColor = ~spatial_slope_pal(combined_slope_mean),
             fillOpacity = 0.8,
             popup = ~text,
             stroke = 0) |>
    addCircleMarkers(data = slopes_spatial_fits,
             fillColor = ~spatial_slope_pal(combined_slope_mean),
             fillOpacity = 0.8,
             popup = ~text,
             stroke = 1) |>
   addLegend(pal =spatial_slope_pal,
             values = seq(domain[1], domain[2], length.out = 7) )






Last, let’s show the data set, but the curves show the regional fits - again, colors go south to north.


Show the code
spatial_curves <- readRDS(here::here("data/model_derived_data/prediction_spatial_model_curves.rds")) |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("X", "Y"), 
           crs = st_crs(spatial_predictions),
           remove = FALSE)|> 
  # crop to the dataset
  st_crop(st_bbox(fitted_spatial_predictions) |>st_as_sfc() |> st_buffer(1e1)) |>
  st_transform(4326) %>%
    mutate(lon = sf::st_coordinates(.)[,1],
                lat = sf::st_coordinates(.)[,2]) |>
  # Trim to the time of the data set
  filter(year >= min(study_data$Sample.Year)) |>
  filter(year <= max(study_data$Sample.Year))


Warning: attribute variables are assumed to be spatially constant throughout
all geometries


Show the code
ggplot(fitted_spatial_predictions,
       aes(x = year, color = latitude,
                    y = yi)) +
  geom_point( alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_line(data = spatial_curves,
            aes(y = est, 
                color = lat,
                group = Y))  +
  scale_color_viridis_c() +
  labs(y="", x = "Standardized Kelp Abundance", 
       color = "Latitude")

text:
4.6 How Does the Data Fit Into the Spatio-Temporal Time Series Model?
First, let’s look at the map showing slopes for each site for each decade.


Show the code
yrs <- c(1975, 1985, 1995, 2005, 2015) + 5


Next, let’s see how that actually plays out on a scatter plot with individual fit lines overlain. Note, colors go from south to north.
The above shows the results directly from the fit model for the individual data sets. These data, however, have a random effect for each site. Let’s instead show a map of the region by decade with the general trends from the region from the model fit.
Last, let’s show the data set, but the curves show the regional fits - again, colors go south to north.
